issue.title: fix(embed): Video unavailable — fetchVideoMetadata never parsed imeta.url
issue.body:
## Problem

The `/embed/{id}` edge handler (Fastly Compute JS) returns "Video unavailable" for all embeds, even when the video exists. The root cause is in `fetchVideoMetadata` in `compute-js/src/index.js` — it never extracted the `.imeta.url` or `.imeta.m` fields from the video API response, so `videoUrl` was always `undefined`.

## Evidence

- Browser testing confirms embed page hits the edge and fetches metadata from funnelcake
- Logs show `title: Hey Houston!` but no `videoUrl` in the metadata
- `renderEmbedPage` receives `videoUrl: undefined` and renders the fallback "Video unavailable" message
- `relay.divine.video/api/oEmbed` returns valid oEmbed JSON for the same video ID — the media itself is fine

## Example Embed URL

- https://divine.video/embed/32686986622f6041ba7d30375135b6ae42c6551fa58d1297acf7074c73863b3e

issue.title: web fallback for invite links on iOS
issue.body:
When someone on iOS taps an invite link from the Divine mobile app and doesn't have the app installed, they hit a 404. The code is lost.

This PR adds a web fallback at /invite/:code that reads the code, validates it against /v1/validate, and shows the user either a pre-filled form or an error state. Submitting the form hands the invite off to the login flow.

Also adds a Smart App Banner for iOS Safari so users without the app get prompted to install it.

Translations across all 16 locales are stubbed in with English placeholders — proper translations can follow once the copy is locked.

Draft PR with full context: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-web/pull/385

issue.title: show login dialog on video page like/repost, not a toast
issue.body:
Everywhere else in the app, tapping like or repost while logged out opens the login dialog. On the video page, it just shows a toast that says "no" and stops there.

This PR wires up the login dialog on the video page too, so unauthenticated users can sign in and complete the action without a second tap.

Draft PR with full context: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-web/pull/378

issue.title: fix(#51): firefox video loading reliability
issue.body:
## Summary

- Reduced unnecessary media auth preflight traffic by running `checkMediaAuth` only for protected, age-restricted media URLs.
- Added short-lived caching and in-flight request deduplication for media auth checks to avoid repeated `HEAD` calls for the same URL.
- Improved Firefox loading behavior by removing forced `crossOrigin="anonymous"` on media elements and limiting Firefox prefetch to image thumbnails (skipping video prefetch).

> Avoid naming corporate partners, customers, or other sensitive external brands in this PR title or body. Use generic descriptors unless a maintainer explicitly approves the public reference.

## Motivation

- Firefox users reported slower and less reliable video loading compared to Chromium-based browsers.
- The feed could trigger avoidable request overhead (auth preflight and video prefetch pressure), which increases startup latency and amplifies browser-specific networking differences.
- This change keeps protected-media behavior intact while reducing unnecessary network work for public media.

## Related Issue

- Closes #51

## Testing

- [ ] `npm run test`
- [ ] Manual verification completed

Additional targeted checks run:
- `npx vitest run src/components/VideoPlayer.test.tsx src/components/ThumbnailPlayer.test.tsx src/hooks/useAdultVerification.test.ts`
- `npx vitest run src/hooks/useVideoPrefetch.test.ts src/components/VideoPlayer.test.tsx src/components/VideoPlayer.authHeaders.test.tsx src/components/ThumbnailPlayer.test.tsx src/components/VideoGrid.test.tsx`

## Visuals

- [ ] UI change with screenshots/video attached
- [x] No visual change
- [x] Visuals and text avoid sensitive external brand or partner names unless explicitly approved

issue.title: Profile video grid loses scroll position when navigating back from a video
issue.body:
## Problem

When a user scrolls deep into a profile's video grid, clicks a video to open it, then navigates back, the grid resets to the top. The user has to re-scroll and the feed re-fetches from page 1.

This is especially painful for moderators triaging a creator's catalog — they lose their place every time they open a video to report it.

## Expected

Returning to the profile page should restore the previous scroll position and the videos that were already loaded, without re-fetching from the start.

## Notes

- Likely needs scroll restoration on the profile videos route and cache preservation of the loaded pages (TanStack Query `gcTime` may already cover the data; the missing piece is scroll position + which pages were loaded).
- Related: if thumbnails were real `<a href>` links, users could middle-click to open in a new tab and sidestep the problem entirely (filed separately).

comment.body:
Hey @jalcine! I've pushed fixes to the same [branch](https://github.com/DSanich/divine-web/tree/fix/379-profile-grid-scroll-restore). Swapped the rAF retry loop for a ResizeObserver so it only fires when the page actually grows, added a 50-entry cap on the scroll map, and wired up pageshow to handle bfcache restores properly.

Re-read CONTRIBUTING.md again too. Quick question — does pulling the deferred restore logic into a separate routeScrollRestoration.ts cross the line as a "new caching layer", or is it fine since it's just scoped to ScrollToTop? Asking because I want to make sure I'm not overstepping before opening the PR.

issue.title: feat: add web fallback for /invite/:code
issue.body:
## Context

When someone shares an invite code from our mobile app — like `ABCD-1234` — the URL that gets constructed is `https://divine.video/invite/ABCD-1234`. This is something we ship as a universal link, meant to open our app if someone's got it installed.

- **Android**: The intent filter in our manifest already handles `/invite/*` with `autoVerify="true"` — the app opens there.  
- **iOS**: We're not updating the AASA — users without the app will fall through to the web page.

The problem: visiting `/invite/:code` on web hit our 404 page. Nothing happened. The code was lost.

## What This Does

### 1. New page at `/invite/:code`
`InvitesLandingPage` reads the code from the URL, validates it against `/v1/validate`, and shows the appropriate state:

| State | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| Valid code | Form pre-filled and ready to submit |
| Invalid code | Error shown, user can still enter their own code |
| Submit | Invite handoff stored in `sessionStorage`, redirect to `login.divine.video` |

The route is placed in `AppRouter` **outside** the auth-gated block, alongside other public routes like `/app/callback` and `/auth/callback`.

### 2. Smart App Banner for iOS
Added `apple-itunes-app` meta tag — when someone visits from Safari on iOS without the app installed, they get the "Download in the App Store" banner.

### 3. i18n across all 16 locales
`src/lib/i18n/locales.test.ts` enforces key parity across all locales. Added 8 new keys (`invitesLandingPage.*`) to all 16 locale files with English placeholder values. Proper translations can follow in a subsequent effort.

## What I'd Like to See Next

- Proper translations for Spanish, French, Portuguese
- Possibly a follow-up to track adoption of the `/invite/:code` path (e.g., analytics event on page load)

issue.title: Profile video grid loses scroll position when navigating back from a video
issue.body:
## Problem

When a user scrolls deep into a profile's video grid, clicks a video to open it, then navigates back, the grid resets to the top. The user has to re-scroll and the feed re-fetches from page 1.

This is especially painful for moderators triaging a creator's catalog — they lose their place every time they open a video to report it.

## Expected

Returning to the profile page should restore the previous scroll position and the videos that were already loaded, without re-fetching from the start.

## Notes

- Likely needs scroll restoration on the profile videos route and cache preservation of the loaded pages (TanStack Query `gcTime` may already cover the data; the missing piece is scroll position + which pages were loaded).
- Related: if thumbnails were real `<a href>` links, users could middle-click to open in a new tab and sidestep the problem entirely (filed separately).

comment.body:
Hey @DSanich, going forward, I _really would recommend_ reading [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-web/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before piping PRs into a LLM for work. In this particular issue, Liz made two good notes that were ignored in your implementation. For example, your changes are cool but they don't consider things like:

- Memory leaking: scrollPositions Map grows unbounded with no cleanup when entries become stale. Horrible for mobile Web experiences.
- `pagehide` reliability: May not fire in [bfcache](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/bfcache) scenarios across all browsers
- 120 frames (~2s) might cause jitter on slow pages (especially older devices; I use a iPhone XR for example and this choked on it).

**Please** read the guidelines and hold a bit more of a rigor with testing; thank you!

issue.title: test(comments): unit tests for NIP-22 comment tags and usePostComment
issue.body:
## Summary

Add **pure unit tests** for **NIP-22 (kind 1111)** tag construction and **hook tests** for **`usePostComment`**, including **`onMutate` / `onSettled`** cache behaviour for `['nostr', 'comments', …]` queries. Comments power threading and Funnelcake indexing — tag mistakes cause **missing threads**, not loud UI errors.

## Problem

- `src/hooks/usePostComment.ts` builds a large conditional matrix: **URL vs event** roots, **addressable vs replaceable** kinds, **reply** vs top-level branch, **NKinds** from `@nostrify/nostrify`.
- Logic is **inline** in `mutationFn` — hard to review and **not** covered by `CommentForm.test.tsx` (that file mocks the hook entirely).
- Wrong **`E`/`A`/`a`/`e`/`P`/`p`/`K`/`k`** combinations are exactly the bugs this suite should prevent.

## Expected outcome

1. **Preferred:** Extract **`buildNip22CommentTags(root, reply, content)`** (or similarly named) into `src/lib/` returning `string[][]`, with **table-driven tests** for representative cases:
   - Addressable **34236** video root with `d` tag → expect **`A`**, **`E`**, **`K`**, **`P`** as in current code.
   - Top-level vs reply: duplicate **`a`/`e`** branch when `reply` is absent (mirror implementation).
   - **URL** roots: **`I`/`i`** tags and hostname-based **`K`/`k`**.
2. **`usePostComment.test.ts`**: mock **`useNostrPublish`**, assert **`publishEvent`** receives built tags; verify **`onMutate`** cancels/updates queries as implemented.

## What needs to be tested

### Pure tag builder (if extracted)

- At minimum **three** fixtures: **video addressable event**, **generic event root**, **URL root**; plus one **reply-to-comment** case if supported by types.
- Snapshot or deep-equal **`tags`** array order — order may matter to some indexers.

### Hook

- **`publishEvent`** invoked with `kind: 1111` and expected tags for each fixture.
- Cache: **`cancelQueries`** / **`invalidateQueries`** keys align with `rootId` derivation (`root.id` vs URL string).

## Mocking strategy

- Construct minimal **`NostrEvent`** objects (id, pubkey, kind, tags, content, created_at, sig) — no relay I/O.
- `vi.mock('@/hooks/useNostrPublish')`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests live next to code or under `src/lib/` for extracted builder + `src/hooks/usePostComment.test.ts`.
- [ ] No network.
- [ ] `npm run test` + `npx tsc --noEmit` pass.

## Related files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/hooks/usePostComment.ts` | Mutation + tag logic |
| `src/components/comments/CommentForm.test.tsx` | Mocks hook — not coverage |

## Notes

- **Out of scope:** full **`useComments`** infinite query tests unless time permits — file a **follow-up issue** if parsing/query filters need coverage too.
- If extraction is rejected by reviewers, document **mutation-only tests** with duplicated expectations — still better than zero coverage.

comment.body:
@jalcine You're right—the problem looks like a checklist, not what I imagined 😅

My goal was to test NIP-22 comment tags in usePostComment. Incorrect E/A/a, etc. often look fine in the UI, but the discussion threads don't display—CommentForm.test.tsx simulates a hook, so it doesn't check anything about what we post.

I was working with a comment stream, read usePostComment.ts (a large matrix of inline tags + caching by ['nostr', 'comments', rootId]), and wanted to block it before refactoring. Extracting it into a task was just one option; hook-only tests would also work, if that's more convenient for you.

I'd be happy to discuss it.

issue.title: test(comments): extract NIP-22 tag builder and add usePostComment tests
issue.body:
## Summary

- Extract **`buildNip22CommentTags(root, reply?)`** into `src/lib/buildNip22CommentTags.ts` — pure NIP-22 (kind **1111**) tag construction previously inlined in **`usePostComment`** (URL vs event roots, addressable/replaceable/regular kinds, reply vs top-level branches).
- Wire **`usePostComment`** to call the helper inside **`mutationFn`** so publish payloads stay identical while logic becomes unit-testable.
- Add **`buildNip22CommentTags.test.ts`** with fixtures for addressable short-video roots (kind **34236**), regular/replaceable roots, URL roots, threaded replies (including reply-as-URL).
- Add **`usePostComment.test.ts`** with mocked **`useNostrPublish`** / **`useCurrentUser`**: asserts **`publishEvent`** receives **`kind: 1111`** and matching tags (including **`reply`**); exercises **`cancelQueries`**, deferred-publish optimistic UI, **`onSuccess`** replacement + **`invalidateQueries`** after the **6s** delay (fake timers), and **`onError`** rollback.

> Avoid naming corporate partners, customers, or other sensitive external brands in this PR title or body. Use generic descriptors unless a maintainer explicitly approves the public reference.

## Motivation

- Comment tag matrices are easy to get wrong; mistakes surface as **missing threads** or indexer mismatches rather than obvious UI errors. **#341** asks for extracted, tested tag construction plus hook coverage for cache/`publishEvent` behaviour.

## Related Issue

- Closes #341

## Testing

- [x] `npm run test`
- [x] Manual verification completed

## Visuals

review.body:
## Review

The core change is right — login dialog instead of toast, matching every other surface in the app. The pending-action auto-execute is a nice UX touch. But the tests are broken and need a fix before merge.

### 1. Both tests fail: missing `LoginDialogContext` mock

`useLoginDialog()` throws on render because there's no `vi.mock('@/contexts/LoginDialogContext')`. This breaks **both** tests, not just the new one — the `openLoginDialogMock` / `closeLoginDialogMock` created via `vi.hoisted()` are never wired to anything.

```
 FAIL  src/pages/VideoPage.test.tsx > VideoPage > navigates through bounded search results while preserving search params
 FAIL  src/pages/VideoPage.test.tsx > VideoPage > clears pending social action when login dialog is dismissed without successful login
Error: useLoginDialog must be used within LoginDialogProvider
  at useLoginDialog src/contexts/LoginDialogContext.tsx:27:11
  at VideoPage src/pages/VideoPage.tsx:210:74
```

Needs something like:
```typescript
vi.mock('@/contexts/LoginDialogContext', () => ({
  useLoginDialog: () => ({
    openLoginDialog: openLoginDialogMock,
    closeLoginDialog: closeLoginDialogMock,
    isOpen: false,
  }),
}));
```

The new test also needs the mock `VideoCard` to wire `onLike` to the button — right now the buttons are static DOM elements with no `onClick`, so clicks never reach `handleLike`.

### 2. Pending action doesn't survive redirect logins

The `useRef` holding the pending action is lost when the primary login paths (`handleExistingAccountLogin`, `handleInviteSubmit`) call `window.location.assign()` — the component unmounts and the ref is gone. When the user returns post-OAuth, they're logged in but need to tap Like again.

Not a regression — the old toast didn't preserve intent either — and the auto-execute does work for in-app logins (extension, nsec, bunker). But the PR description promises "one intent, one flow, no second tap needed" which only holds for those advanced methods. The default register and sign-in tabs both redirect. Worth either scoping the description or stashing the intent in `sessionStorage` for a future pass.

### 3. Minor cleanup

- `closeLoginDialog` is destructured at line 210 but never used.
- The three `videoPage.loginRequired*` i18n keys (`loginRequiredTitle`, `loginRequiredLikeDescription`, `loginRequiredRepostDescription`) are now dead across all locale files — safe to remove here or in a follow-up.

issue.title: Video thumbnails can't be opened in a new tab (middle-click / right-click)
issue.body:
## Problem

On the web app, video thumbnails in the profile grid (and likely other feeds) don't support standard browser behaviors:

- Middle-click / scroll-wheel-click doesn't open the video in a new tab
- Right-click → \"Open in new tab\" isn't offered

This blocks a common power-user workflow — opening several videos into background tabs to review them without losing scroll position in the source feed. A moderator triaging a creator's catalog hit this directly.

## Expected

Thumbnails behave like native links: middle-click and right-click → \"Open link in new tab\" both work.

## Notes

- Likely cause: thumbnails are clickable `<div>`/`<button>`s with `onClick` navigation instead of real `<a href>` elements. Switching to anchor-based navigation (or wrapping the clickable area in `<a>`) restores native browser behavior for free.
- Audit other feed surfaces (home, trending, search results) for the same pattern while we're in there.

issue.title: Profile video grid stops loading more videos when scrolling deep on web
issue.body:
## Problem

On the web app, scrolling through a profile's video grid eventually stops loading new videos — the feed stalls before reaching the end of the creator's catalog.

Reported by a user trying to scroll through a large set of a single creator's videos.

## Expected

Infinite scroll should continue paginating until there are no more videos for that profile.

## Notes

- Needs repro: which profile, how many videos deep before it stalls, console/network errors at the stall point.
- Suspect areas: the profile videos pagination hook, end-of-feed sentinel logic, or a Funnelcake cursor/limit issue. Check whether the circuit breaker is opening mid-scroll and the WebSocket fallback is terminating early.

issue.title: Profile video grid loses scroll position when navigating back from a video
issue.body:
## Problem

When a user scrolls deep into a profile's video grid, clicks a video to open it, then navigates back, the grid resets to the top. The user has to re-scroll and the feed re-fetches from page 1.

This is especially painful for moderators triaging a creator's catalog — they lose their place every time they open a video to report it.

## Expected

Returning to the profile page should restore the previous scroll position and the videos that were already loaded, without re-fetching from the start.

## Notes

- Likely needs scroll restoration on the profile videos route and cache preservation of the loaded pages (TanStack Query `gcTime` may already cover the data; the missing piece is scroll position + which pages were loaded).
- Related: if thumbnails were real `<a href>` links, users could middle-click to open in a new tab and sidestep the problem entirely (filed separately).

issue.title: feat(#86): support ticket creation parity with mobile
issue.body:
## Summary

This PR finishes the remaining work for divine-web issue #86 and brings the web app much closer to the Zendesk reporting behavior already established in divine-mobile.

A good amount of the foundation for this issue had already been put in place by @mbradley. In particular, the web app already had a `/api/report` path and an existing Zendesk-backed content-report flow. This PR builds on that work by adding the missing structured bug-report flow on the web client, extending the backend to support bug tickets, and tightening parity for content-report payloads as well.

It also includes a small follow-up pass on local developer experience, because during testing it became clear that the original implementation could not be exercised through plain Vite dev mode without extra Fastly setup.

## What Was Already Done By @mbradley

Before this PR, the following pieces were already in place:

- the web app already had a report backend exposed through `/api/report`
- content reports were already wired into Zendesk
- the Fastly implementation in `compute-js/src/index.js` and the Cloudflare Pages implementation in `functions/api/report.ts` were already serving as the report backend foundation
- the issue had already been partially solved on the backend side, especially for content-report routing

This PR does not replace that work. It completes the missing pieces on top of it.

## What This PR Adds

### Structured bug reporting on the web
This PR adds a proper bug-report flow to divine-web from the Support page, including:

- a new `BugReportDialog`
- a `useBugReport` hook
- bug-report support in `src/lib/reportApi.ts`
- support for both signed-in reporters and guest reporters via email fallback

### Zendesk bug ticket support in `/api/report`
The report backend now accepts `reportType: 'bug'` and creates structured Zendesk bug tickets with the same general field model used by divine-mobile.

That includes support for:

- Zendesk bug ticket form ID
- Ticket Type = `incident`
- Platform
- OS Version
- Build Number
- Steps to Reproduce
- Expected Behavior

Both backend implementations were updated:

- `compute-js/src/index.js`
- `functions/api/report.ts`

### Web metadata capture
Bug reports now automatically include useful web-specific context such as:

- current page URL
- browser user agent
- app version
- inferred OS string from the user agent

### Support page entry point
The Support page now includes a visible “Report a bug” entry point so the flow is reachable in the product without depending on the old Zendesk widget flow.

### Content-report parity improvements
While implementing the bug flow, this PR also improves the existing content-report payload so it is closer to the mobile behavior and more internally consistent.

That includes:

- requester name parity
- `external_id` for authenticated reporters
- `nip-56` and `web` tags
- a clearer “Reported via Divine web” marker in the ticket body

### Test coverage
This PR adds focused tests for:

- bug report payload formatting
- the bug-report hook
- the Support page entry point
- backend Zendesk payload generation

## Local Testing Notes

The UI flow can be tested locally, and the request path can now be exercised locally through Vite + Fastly local setup.

However, full end-to-end validation of real Zendesk ticket creation is still not possible in my current environment because I do not have the required Zendesk credentials available locally.

Specifically, successful ticket creation depends on:

- `ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN`
- `ZENDESK_API_EMAIL`
- `ZENDESK_API_TOKEN`

Without those values, the local report backend can start, but the request will fail at the Zendesk configuration step rather than creating a real ticket.

So in practice, this PR has been validated as far as local app behavior, payload construction, backend routing, and error handling allow, but final confirmation of real Zendesk ticket creation still needs to happen in an environment where the Zendesk variables are available.

issue.title: fix(#280): align e/p tag report types with nip 56 standard values
issue.body:
## Summary

- Align report event `e/p` tag third values with NIP-56 standard report types.
- Preserve app-level report categorization via existing NIP-32 `L/l` tags (`social.nos.ontology`, `NS-*`).
- Add targeted tests for mapping correctness and report tag contract on kind `1984` events.

## Problem

`useReportContent()` was writing app-level reasons (for example `csam`, `sexual-content`, `harassment`) directly into the `e/p` tag third element.

NIP-56 requires these values to be one of:
`nudity`, `malware`, `profanity`, `illegal`, `spam`, `impersonation`, `other`.

## What Changed

- Added an explicit mapping from `ContentFilterReason` to NIP-56 report types.
- Updated `useReportContent()` to use mapped NIP-56 values in:
  - `["e", "<eventId>", "<nip56-type>"]`
  - `["p", "<pubkey>", "<nip56-type>"]`
- Kept NIP-32 label tags unchanged so app-level semantics remain queryable:
  - `["L", "social.nos.ontology"]`
  - `["l", "NS-<app-reason>", "social.nos.ontology"]`
- Added unit tests covering:
  - full mapping table
  - published report tags for kind `1984`
  - regression checks to ensure raw app-level reasons are not used in `e/p`

## Related

- https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-web/issues/280
- https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3492
- https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-relay-manager/pull/50

Closes #280

issue.title: test(comments): unit tests for NIP-22 comment tags and usePostComment
issue.body:
## Summary

Add **pure unit tests** for **NIP-22 (kind 1111)** tag construction and **hook tests** for **`usePostComment`**, including **`onMutate` / `onSettled`** cache behaviour for `['nostr', 'comments', …]` queries. Comments power threading and Funnelcake indexing — tag mistakes cause **missing threads**, not loud UI errors.

## Problem

- `src/hooks/usePostComment.ts` builds a large conditional matrix: **URL vs event** roots, **addressable vs replaceable** kinds, **reply** vs top-level branch, **NKinds** from `@nostrify/nostrify`.
- Logic is **inline** in `mutationFn` — hard to review and **not** covered by `CommentForm.test.tsx` (that file mocks the hook entirely).
- Wrong **`E`/`A`/`a`/`e`/`P`/`p`/`K`/`k`** combinations are exactly the bugs this suite should prevent.

## Expected outcome

1. **Preferred:** Extract **`buildNip22CommentTags(root, reply, content)`** (or similarly named) into `src/lib/` returning `string[][]`, with **table-driven tests** for representative cases:
   - Addressable **34236** video root with `d` tag → expect **`A`**, **`E`**, **`K`**, **`P`** as in current code.
   - Top-level vs reply: duplicate **`a`/`e`** branch when `reply` is absent (mirror implementation).
   - **URL** roots: **`I`/`i`** tags and hostname-based **`K`/`k`**.
2. **`usePostComment.test.ts`**: mock **`useNostrPublish`**, assert **`publishEvent`** receives built tags; verify **`onMutate`** cancels/updates queries as implemented.

## What needs to be tested

### Pure tag builder (if extracted)

issue.title: refactor(profile): extract and test metadata normalization in EditProfileForm
issue.body:
## Summary
Extract the profile metadata merge/cleanup logic from `EditProfileForm` into a pure helper and cover it with focused tests.

## Problem
The save path currently normalizes profile metadata inline inside `onSubmit`. PR #289 added important `display_name` synchronization logic there, but the behavior is still embedded in the component and untested.

## Expected fix
- Extract the metadata normalization into a pure helper
- Add unit tests that cover at least:
  - `display_name` mirrors `name` when `name` is present
  - `display_name` is removed when `name` is cleared
  - empty-string fields are removed before publish
  - existing metadata is preserved when not overwritten by form values

## Context
Follow-up from PR #289.
